Explanation

Your application has hardcoded URLs that might correspond to services that are not accessible on Azure.

Review and ensure that the application is attempting to access URLs that would be available from Azure. You might need to migrate those services to Azure too, this way you will get the benefit of lower latency in the cloud.

If your application needs to depend on services that run on-premises, you can connect your Azure and local networks with ExpressRoute, Hybrid Connections, or VPN solutions.
Local or network IO operations detected
 Potential 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.csLine 57
src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.csLine 57

Explanation

Your application has local or network IO operations.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, move persistent I/O to storage mounts (Azure Files/UNC). Keep local writes to temp only; connect to external dependencies via private endpoints/VNet to reduce latency.

IO operations outside of the application folder might not be available on Azure App Service. Review and ensure IO APIs are attempting to access paths that will be available when your app is running on App Service sandbox. If you choose the containerized hosting option, your scenario still might be broken or have scalability issues.

Possible solutions:
1. Files that the application needs can be deployed with the application or put in Azure Storage. You can use Azure Storage File Shares as a drop-in replacement for on-premises file share.
2. Other services that the application depends on might need to be migrated to Azure, this way you will get the benefit of lower latency in the cloud.
3. If your application needs to depend on services that run on-premise, you can connect your Azure and local networks with ExpressRoute, Hybrid Connections, or VPN solutions.
Local OS environment access detected
 Potential 1
FilePosition
src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.csLine 56
src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.csLine 56

Explanation

Local OS environment access detected.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, Read config via App Settings or App Configuration; avoid machine‑specific environment APIs. Persist environment setup via install scripts when needed.

When running in Azure App Service environment, your application can read environment variables that you define in App Service settings. Using environment API other than reading environment variables might indicate that your application depends on some local machine's features and might be broken on App Service sandbox or not scale well. Review your scenarios and either refactor them to be more cloud friendly or choose the option in App Service to host your application in the sandbox for Windows Container Web Apps.

If you choose to use other Azure hosting options such as Azure Container Apps (ACA) or Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), environment APIs might work, however scaling still might be an issue.
SQL database connection detected
 Potential 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\Web.config

Explanation

SQL database connection detected.

Ensure the database is available/reachable on Azure.

If it is not, there are multiple ways you can move your data to Azure:
1. Migrate to Azure SQL Database.
2. Consider Azure SQL Managed Instance if you need features that are not available in Azure SQL Database and you don’t want to use a VM.
3. Migrate your database servers directly to SQL Server on Azure VMs.

To assess database migration effort, you can use Azure Migrate tool, see the link below.

Explanation

Connection strings without configuration builders detected.

Keeping connection strings directly in the app is not the best practice and might introduce security risks, increased maintenance, scalability challenges or compliance standards (such as PCI DSS, GDPR, etc.).

Instead, it is recommended to use configuration builders to get secrets from secure sources in Azure environment.

Your current approach of serving static content directly might lead to increased costs, performance issues, maintenance challenges (requiring application redeployment for content changes), and security risks.

Consider moving static content to Azure Blob Storage and adding Azure CDN.
Upgrade to newer target framework to get better cloud experience
 Optional 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\eShopWCFService.csproj

Explanation

Upgrade to newer target framework to get better cloud experience.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, validate on .NET Framework 4.8 or move to .NET 10. Persist any runtime prerequisites via install scripts; test in staging before production.

While if targeting other Azure compute services:

Application targeting .NET framework lower than 4.7.1 might missing features that would be needed for some cloud scenarios like scaling or getting secrets from secure external sources.

Azure App Service runs apps on .NET Framework 4.8 or .NET Framework 3.5. Apps running on on .NET Framework versions older than .NET Framework 4.8 could have potential compatibility issues. It is recommended to test your application running on .NET Framework 4.8. Note that it is not necessary to re-target to .NET Framework 4.8, only to validate that the app correctly runs on that version of .NET Framework.

In the long term it is also recommended to upgrade your application to latest supported .NET 8+ which would significantly increase performance of your application. Use tools like .NET Upgrade Assistant to help with upgrading your application to newer .NET.
System.Data.SqlClient dependency detected
 Optional 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\Web.config

Explanation

System.Data.SqlClient dependency is detected.

While System.Data.SqlClient will work in Azure, the newer Microsoft.Data.SqlClient package is the primary .NET SQL client moving forward and receiving the latest features. For example, Microsoft.Data.SqlClient easily allows use of Azure Managed Identity from a connection string.

Explanation

API is binary incompatible for selected .NET version: affects existing binaries, often requiring recompilation, because the API has changed in a way that prevents older binaries from loading or executing.
Project's target framework(s) needs to be changed
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\eShopWCFService.csproj
src\eShopWinForms\eShopWinForms.csproj

Explanation

Project's target framework(s) needs to be changed to the new target framework that you selected for this upgrade.

During upgrade target framework will be adjusted to corresponding platform when applicable. In some cases project would result in multiple target frameworks after the upgrade if it was using features that now have their own platforms in modern .NET frameworks (windows, iOS, Android etc).
Project file needs to be converted to SDK-style
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\eShopWCFService.csproj

Explanation

Project file needs to be converted to SDK-style. Modern .NET framework projects require a change in the project file format and use SDK corresponding to project flavor and functionality.
WCF Client APIs
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition

Explanation

WCF client-side APIs for building service clients that communicate with WCF services. These APIs are available as exact equivalents via NuGet packages - add System.ServiceModel.* NuGet packages (System.ServiceModel.Http, System.ServiceModel.Primitives, System.ServiceModel.NetTcp, etc.)
Legacy Configuration System
 Mandatory 2
FilePosition

Explanation

Legacy XML-based configuration system (app.config/web.config) that has been replaced by a more flexible configuration model in .NET Core. The old system was rigid and XML-based. Migrate to Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration with JSON/environment variables; use System.Configuration.ConfigurationManager NuGet package as interim bridge if needed.
GDI+ / System.Drawing
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition

Explanation

System.Drawing APIs for 2D graphics, imaging, and printing that are available via NuGet package System.Drawing.Common. Note: Not recommended for server scenarios due to Windows dependencies; consider cross-platform alternatives like SkiaSharp or ImageSharp for new code.
Windows Forms Legacy Controls
 Mandatory 3
FilePosition

Explanation

Legacy Windows Forms controls that have been removed from .NET Core/5+ including StatusBar, DataGrid, ContextMenu, MainMenu, MenuItem, and ToolBar. These controls were replaced by more modern alternatives. Use ToolStrip, MenuStrip, ContextMenuStrip, and DataGridView instead.
Windows Forms
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition

Explanation

Architecture Diagram

Source assessment of D:\a\eShopModernizing\eShopModernizing\eShopModernizedNTier only. The solution contains a Windows desktop client and an IIS-hosted WCF catalog service; SQL Server is the external persistence dependency ([solution][solution], [deployment][compose]).

Data Storage & External Services

All five entity sets are owned by the WCF service. An environment-supplied connection selects SQL Server in Compose; otherwise EF resolves the named LocalDB connection. These are alternatives, not replicated databases. The desktop loads catalog images from local files; there is no discovered object-storage service, message broker, remote business API, or distributed cache. See [DbContext][model], [connection resolution][connection] and [image loading][view].

Key Architectural Decisions

  • A desktop controller coordinates the view and generated WCF proxy; Program.Main wires them manually. The commented registration code in ApplicationModule is not an active DI container ([composition][program], [module][module]).
  • The service implements the contract and queries EntityModel directly, without a separate repository or domain-service tier ([contract][contract], [implementation][service]).
  • Database initialization is create-if-absent with programmatic seed data; it is not a migration pipeline ([initializer][seed]).

API & Service Communication Contracts

The scoped application exposes 10 SOAP operations on one WCF service endpoint, not ten REST URLs. Its desktop client performs synchronous request/reply calls; generated async methods are alternatives, not broker-based messaging ([contract][contract], [controller][controller]).

Service Catalog

ServicePortCategoryPurpose
eShopWCFService / eshopwcfserviceContainer 80; host 5113; IIS development URL uses 5200BusinessCatalog and inventory SOAP service; WCF and EF6
eShopWinFormsNo listening service portClient, outside API/Business/Infrastructure server categoriesDesktop consumer; Windows Forms and WCF client packages
sql.dataContainer 1433; host 5433InfrastructureThird-party SQL Server container; not a source-built business service

The solution and Compose identify these boundaries; no gateway, service registry or separate observability service is defined ([solution][solution], [Compose][compose], [override][override], [IIS settings][iis], [desktop manifest][desktop]).

API Endpoints Inventory

All operations use POST /CatalogService.svc, with the operation selected through SOAPAction rather than a REST path. SOAP actions have the prefix http://tempuri.org/ICatalogService/ plus the operation name, as confirmed by the generated proxy. There is no explicit API versioning ([binding][web], [generated contract][proxycontract]).

ServiceMethodPathRequest TypeResponse Type
CatalogServicePOST / SOAP FindCatalogItem/CatalogService.svcint id in SOAP bodyCatalogItem, or null when absent
CatalogServicePOST / SOAP GetCatalogBrandsSame endpointEmpty operation bodyList; proxy CatalogBrand[]
CatalogServicePOST / SOAP GetCatalogItemsSame endpointint brandIdFilter, int typeIdFilterList; proxy CatalogItem[]
CatalogServicePOST / SOAP GetCatalogTypesSame endpointEmpty operation bodyList; proxy CatalogType[]
CatalogServicePOST / SOAP GetAvailableStockSame endpointDateTime date, int catalogItemIdint; zero when no matching record
CatalogServicePOST / SOAP CreateAvailableStockSame endpointCatalogItemsStockVoid reply
CatalogServicePOST / SOAP CreateCatalogItemSame endpointCatalogItemVoid reply; allocated ID is not returned
CatalogServicePOST / SOAP UpdateCatalogItemSame endpointCatalogItemVoid reply
CatalogServicePOST / SOAP RemoveCatalogItemSame endpointCatalogItemVoid reply; see implementation caveat below
CatalogServicePOST / SOAP GetDiscountSame endpointDateTime dayDiscountItem, or null when none applies

Normal SOAP request/reply success uses HTTP 200; unhandled service exceptions use WCF SOAP fault behavior, typically HTTP 500, rather than custom REST 400/404 contracts. No [FaultContract], explicit HTTP status mapping or declared validation-fault DTO exists. Null item and missing-stock results are normal replies, not HTTP 404 responses. RemoveCatalogItem passes the deserialized entity directly to DbSet.Remove without attaching or fetching it; successful deletion of a detached remote object is not established by the implementation ([implementation][service]).

Metadata configuration is in [Web.config][web]. SQL's Compose healthcheck is an internal command, not an application management API; see configuration-inventory.md.

DTOs & Contracts

  • CatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogType, CatalogItemsStock and DiscountItem are mutable service-owned EF entity/data-contract classes. They double as wire models; there are no gateway aggregation DTOs or immutable record contracts ([entity example][entity], [contract][contract]).
  • WCF uses [DataContract] / [DataMember] XML serialization. The generated desktop namespace is eShopWinForms.eShopServiceReference; collection returns are arrays and it generates both synchronous and task-based methods ([proxy contract][proxycontract]).
  • FilterEventArgs, AvailabilityEventArgs, SearchStockEventArgs are local UI event payloads, not network DTOs ([view contract][viewcontract]).
  • Metadata is exposed dynamically by WCF. No checked-in OpenAPI document, protobuf schema or GraphQL schema was found. See data-architecture.md for entity fields and mappings, and business-workflows.md for validation rules.

Communication Patterns

  • Synchronous: desktop controller → generated WCF proxy → SOAP service → direct EF calls. Although async proxy methods exist, the actual controller calls their synchronous counterparts on the UI execution path ([controller][controller], [startup][program]).
  • Asynchronous: no broker, event bus, background message handler or distributed workflow was discovered.
  • Resilience: no application retry, circuit breaker, bulkhead, fallback response, custom fault recovery or explicit timeout override was found. The generated binding inherits WCF defaults (normally open/send 1 minute, close 1 minute, receive 10 minutes; these are framework defaults, not project-defined policies). Receive timeout is not a client-side retry policy. The generated client increases message/buffer limits to int.MaxValue, uses maximum XML quotas and allows cookies ([generated binding][proxybinding]).
  • Discovery / routing: a hardcoded localhost address is chosen by the generated default constructor. There is no dynamic discovery or client-side load balancing. Compose's SQL service name is a database hostname, not a registry.
  • Gateway composition: none. The desktop combines catalog and discount results from the same backend to render prices; it is not an independently deployed API gateway.
  • Startup availability: desktop initial data loading precedes the visible dialog. Database readiness can affect service requests; Compose startup order alone does not guarantee readiness. Details are in configuration-inventory.md.
  • API security posture: actual client traffic is plain HTTP with a default basicHttpBinding. No API credentials, authenticated principal checks, roles or resource authorization appear in the contract/implementation. HTTPS protocol mapping and HTTPS metadata are declared, but transport TLS is not enforced on the explicit HTTP endpoint or configured desktop connection. Do not infer a working HTTPS deployment from metadata flags ([Web.config][web], [proxy binding and address][proxybinding]).

No JVM applies. No ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT, managed-heap tuning, cloud instance SKU, Kubernetes resources or autoscaling policy is defined. Development service project contains IIS Express enablement, auto port assignment and development-server port 62314; its IIS development address uses port 5200, distinct from Compose and the generated client's 5113 ([service development settings][iis]).

Startup Dependency Chain

  1. External Windows nat network must exist before Compose can attach the containers; these YAML files reference it rather than create it.
  2. sql.data → WCF container start ordering: root Compose declares depends_on: sql.data. This is not a health-conditioned dependency in the shown version-3.4 definition.
  3. SQL readiness observation: root override runs sqlcmd with a masked credential and select 1; interval 1 second, retries 20. No explicit start period or healthcheck timeout is set. The alternate CI file also specifies 20 retries; the alternate override leaves retries implicit. No explicit wait/retry code connects this health result to WCF request handling.
  4. WCF → database on use: EF initialization can create/seed a missing database during data access. No startup migration job, dockerize loop or service readiness endpoint is provided.
  5. Desktop → WCF before dialog display: Program.Main loads initial data synchronously before showing the form. There is no readiness wait or exception-recovery flow; the service and database need to be usable for initial loading.

Evidence: [Compose dependency][compose], [network and healthcheck][override], [alternate CI healthcheck][ci], [initializer registration][context], [desktop startup][program]. No health/management HTTP path is duplicated here.

SQL Server independently receives its password through its environment. No scoped pipeline retrieves secrets, replaces the masked connection placeholder, provisions identity/RBAC, or synchronizes the connection credentials with SQL's administrator secret. Core Business Workflows

The scoped application lets users browse merchandise by brand/type, see currently discounted prices, inspect stock for a chosen day, and record expected stock availability. It does not implement shopping baskets, checkout, payment, shipping execution or customer identity workflows.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalogService / Merchandise catalogSellable merchandise displayed with local image and priceClassified by one brand and one type; referenced by dated stock records
CatalogBrandCatalogService / Catalog taxonomyBrand filter choicesShared by catalog items
CatalogTypeCatalogService / Catalog taxonomyMerchandise-category filter choicesShared by catalog items
CatalogItemsStockCatalogService / Inventory availabilityQuantity expected to be available for an item on a calendar dayLogically references a catalog item
DiscountItemCatalogService / PromotionsGlobal promotion applicable during a date windowApplied to displayed prices; not tied to a specific product

Evidence: [service decisions][service], [desktop coordination][controller], [view behavior][view]. Persistence field lists and mapping details are in data-architecture.md.

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopWCFServiceCatalog, taxonomy, inventory and promotion rules in one serviceAll five domain entitiesOne SQL Server/LocalDB database
eShopWinFormsUser interaction and display compositionNo authoritative persisted domain entitiesWCF service; local image assets
sql.dataPersistence infrastructure, not a business contextHosts service-owned dataWindows container runtime

There are logical concerns inside a single service, not independently deployed bounded-context microservices. The service is authoritative for catalog and stock state; the desktop alone calculates the displayed discounted amount ([program][program], [controller][controller], [view][view]).

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse filtered catalog with current promotion

  1. Startup constructs the view, real proxy and controller, then calls LoadView before showing the dialog. The controller loads the banner, catalog, brand/type selectors and shipment product selectors ([startup][program], [load sequence][controller]).
  2. Selecting a brand/type emits a view event. CatalogController clears the grid and requests matching items using the optional-filter rule.
  3. The service reads catalog data and applies the requested selections; this filtering occurs after materialization.
  4. The controller separately asks for the current promotion using the desktop's local clock. The promotion-window rule selects the first applicable discount.
  5. The view applies the display-price rule and loads the thumbnail corresponding to each product. Prices are not persisted back to the service.
  6. No discount is an ordinary condition: render full prices. A failed SOAP/database call or missing image has no implemented fallback or retry; the grid may already have been cleared.

Evidence: [filter handlers and price rendering][view], [controller catalog/discount calls][controller], [service filters][service].

Workflow 2: Record expected stock for an item and day

  1. The user selects a product and enters quantity and arrival date.
  2. The view applies the shipment-entry presence/parsing rule and emits an availability event.
  3. The controller creates a CatalogItemsStock request and calls the service.
  4. The service looks for the first record matching item and calendar day. If one exists it replaces that day's quantity; this is not an additive shipment ledger. Otherwise it allocates a new identifier and inserts.
  5. After SaveChanges and the SOAP call return, the view displays the success message and clears the entry controls. No success is displayed before the remote write completes.

Evidence: [entry and success UI][view], [request construction][controller], [stock upsert][service]. No domain compensation or duplicate-submission coordination is implemented.

Workflow 3: Look up date-specific availability

  1. The user selects a catalog item from the shipment list and a calendar date.
  2. The view parses the selected item's display string and raises a stock-search event.
  3. The controller requests availability from the service.
  4. The service uses the stock-match rule; when no row exists, it returns zero.
  5. The view appends a result row containing the requested day, product and returned quantity. Repeated searches append rather than replace results.

Evidence: [search and result display][view], [controller lookup][controller], [service lookup][service].

Workflow 4: Initialize a new catalog database

On first EF initialization against an absent database, CatalogDBInitializer seeds taxonomy, merchandise, date-specific inventory and historical promotions. It is not a recurring import, scheduler or event-driven process. Existing databases are not reset or refreshed. Historical seed discounts end in 2017, so they do not create a current promotion on the assessment date ([initializer][initializer], [seed dates][seeds]).

The service additionally declares item create/update/remove operations, but the provided desktop controller does not expose an item-maintenance workflow. They must not be described as working catalog-edit screens. No scheduler or event listener was found.

Cross-Service Data Flows

There is one remote business-service boundary: desktop → CatalogService. The desktop joins catalog results with a separate global discount result to compute display prices and joins product IDs to locally stored image files. It does not aggregate multiple backends, persist joined state, or publish events. Stock operations traverse the same service and database.

There is no circuit-breaker degraded mode. A null discount means no promotion, not a service-outage fallback; zero stock means no matching row or an actual zero quantity, not an infrastructure fallback. The actual composition selects the real generated client; the compiled mock is not wired into startup ([program][program], [controller][controller]).

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant User participant View as "Catalog view" participant Controller as "Desktop controller" participant Service as "Catalog service" participant Store as "Inventory persistence" User->>View: Submit expected quantity and arrival date alt Required input is missing View-->>User: Leave form unchanged without saving else Inputs present and parse successfully View->>Controller: Availability event Controller->>Service: Record stock availability Service->>Store: Find record for item and calendar day alt Existing day record found Store-->>Service: Existing stock record Service->>Store: Replace quantity and save else No day record found Store-->>Service: No matching stock record Service->>Store: Allocate identifier and insert quantity end Store-->>Service: Save completed Service-->>Controller: Operation completed Controller->>View: Confirm availability updated View-->>User: Show success and clear input fields end Note over View,Store: Invalid formats or remote failures have no business fallback or compensation

Business Rules & Decision Logic

RuleActual decision / limitationEvidence
Optional catalog filtersFilter ID zero means “All”; nonzero brand and type restrictions are ANDed. Desktop adds its own “All” entry to lookup lists.[Controller][controller], [service][service]
Promotion windowInclusive comparison of calendar dates; first matching record wins with no explicit ordering, overlap priority or stacking. Caller supplies date; desktop uses DateTime.Now.[Service][service], [controller][controller]
Display priceConvert catalog decimal price to double, multiply by 1 - discount.Size, format with a literal dollar sign and fixed-point text. No persisted sale price, tax or checkout total. Banner percentage is rounded from fraction × 100.[View][view], [controller][controller]
Shipment-entry presence/parsingProduct must be selected; quantity/date strings must be nonempty, otherwise silently return. int.Parse and Convert.ToDateTime parse without a handled format-error path. No nonnegative quantity or future-date restriction appears.[View][view]
Stock search selectionSelected display item is dereferenced and parsed without a null-selection guard in the handler. Calendar selection supplies a day.[View][view]
Stock-match / replacementMatch by item ID and date only; first matching row is used. Existing quantity is overwritten rather than incremented; missing lookup returns zero.[Service][service]
Identifier allocationCatalog and new stock inserts use table maximum plus one. No explicit serialization, empty-table fallback or concurrency coordination around allocation.[Service][service]
Data annotationsBrand and type text each have maximum length 50. No application Required, stock range, price range or discount fraction/date-order validation is declared. EF annotations do not constitute a service-level validation/fault protocol.[Brand][brand], [type][type], [item][item], [stock][stock], [discount][discount]
Item maintenanceCreate adds, update marks supplied entity modified, remove directly removes the supplied entity; no ownership check or domain lifecycle state machine. Detached removal success is not established.[Service][service]
TransactionsEach write calls SaveChanges; no explicit multi-operation transaction, saga or compensation. ID selection and later insert are not protected by a project-defined allocation transaction.[Service][service]
Error handling / auditNo custom business exception/fault contract, retry, dead-letter processing or business audit trail found. Generated service behavior suppresses exception detail in faults.[Contract][contract], [service][service], [WCF behavior][web]
AuthorizationNo business roles, resource-owner checks or permission decisions appear in actual controller/service methods.[Controller][controller], [service][service]

No order states or checkout lifecycle transitions exist in this scoped domain.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The selected desktop targets .NET 6 and the service targets .NET Framework 4.6.1, both past their support windows at this assessment date (2026-10-26). The retained 4.7.1 desktop file and 4.7.2 service container do not change those selected project targets. EF6 versions differ between projects; a move to EF Core is not a package-only replacement. WCF client packages do not provide a modern .NET WCF server host. The unpinned SQL Server container image does not identify a reproducible engine version. These are compatibility observations, not a CVE assessment.

Notable Observations

  • The solution selects eShopWinForms.csproj, not eShopWinForms.fx.csproj; the latter's older versions are not active solution package selections ([solution][solution]).
  • There are no scoped Directory.Packages.props, central version catalog, package lock files or visible resolved dependency graph. Transitive dependencies cannot be enumerated reliably from these manifests; do not infer them from package names.
  • EF6 is explicitly declared in the desktop as well as the service. Manifest analysis alone establishes declaration, not runtime use.
  • No declared messaging, distributed caching, observability, DI-container or resilience packages were found. Framework assemblies are not silently treated as independent NuGet packages.

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

The scoped data layer has five EF6 entity sets persisted to SQL Server or its LocalDB development alternative. The service directly owns its DbContext; the desktop consumes serialized service contracts rather than a separate persistence API ([context][context], [startup][program]).

eShopWCFServiceSQL Server Windows Developer containerRoot Compose environment overrideSame driver/providerEnvironment-provided SQL connection to the database container; credentials [MASKED]Same initializer and seed logic
eShopWinFormsNone directly used by actual startup/controllerDesktopWCF client; EF package also declaredCalls service; no desktop DbContext instantiated in active pathNone

Connection selection is implemented by [CatalogConfiguration][connection]; provider and fallback are in [Web.config][web]. See configuration-inventory.md for property names and raw non-sensitive defaults.

EntityModel registers the initializer in its constructor. Database creation and seeding are deferred to EF initialization on use, not an explicit schema migration job. The initializer adds types, brands, items, stock and discounts and calls SaveChanges separately for each group. No checked-in migrations, schema-versioning scripts or explicit custom pooling configuration were found. Seeds contain 12 catalog items, 5 brands, 4 types, 6 date-specific stock rows and 6 historical discount windows ([initializer][initializer], [seed source][seeds]).

Entity Model

erDiagram %% All persisted entities are owned by eShopWCFService CatalogBrand ||--o{ CatalogItem : "classifies by brand" CatalogType ||--o{ CatalogItem : "classifies by type" CatalogItem ||..o{ CatalogItemsStock : "logical item reference only" CatalogBrand { int Id PK "application assigned" string Brand "maximum length 50; non Unicode" } CatalogType { int Id PK "application assigned" string Type "maximum length 50; non Unicode" } CatalogItem { int Id PK "application assigned" string Description string Name decimal Price "money annotation; precision 19 scale 4" string Picturefilename int CatalogBrandId FK int CatalogTypeId FK } CatalogItemsStock { int StockId PK "application assigned" date Date int CatalogItemId "logical reference; no configured FK" int AvailableStock } DiscountItem { int Id PK "identity by EF convention" double Size date Start date End }

The dotted stock relationship is a logical association used by queries, not an asserted database foreign key: stock has a scalar item ID but no navigation property or explicit relationship mapping. Item→brand and item→type are unidirectional navigations with non-null integer FKs; no inverse collections or custom cascade configuration appear. Convention-driven cascade behavior is not overridden. Navigation properties are not virtual, so lazy-loading proxies are not established by these declarations; FindCatalogItem explicitly loads its two lookup objects ([item][item], [stock][stock], [find behavior][service]).

EntitySourcePersistence details
CatalogBrand[CatalogBrand.cs][brand]Non-generated integer key; optional string of length at most 50; non-Unicode fluent mapping
CatalogType[CatalogType.cs][type]Non-generated integer key; optional string of length at most 50; non-Unicode fluent mapping
CatalogItem[CatalogItem.cs][item]Non-generated integer key; three text descriptors plus image filename; money price; brand/type scalar FKs and navigations
CatalogItemsStock[CatalogItemsStock.cs][stock]Explicit table name and primary key; SQL date; quantity; scalar item reference without mapped navigation
DiscountItem[DiscountItem.cs][discount]Convention-generated key; double fraction; start/end SQL dates; no item FK, so discounts are global

All entity properties are mutable. No concurrency token, unique composite item/date index, field encryption annotation, explicit TransactionScope, or application-managed transaction appears in the mappings. Each mutation calls SaveChanges; EF supplies its ordinary per-save transactional behavior, not a multi-operation service transaction. See business-workflows.md for validation and business decisions.

Caching Strategy

No Redis, distributed cache, MemoryCache, explicit query cache or EF second-level cache configuration was discovered. EF's ordinary context-level entity tracking is not a shared cache or an application TTL policy. Materializing results with ToList does not establish caching across requests. The compiled mock holds in-memory seed lists, but actual desktop composition uses the generated remote client, not this mock ([service][service], [mock][mock], [program][program]). No cache TTL, region, invalidation or session-cache behavior can therefore be attributed to the deployed path.

Data Ownership Boundaries

There is one service-owned database, not database-per-microservice or independently owned databases shared across multiple business services. LocalDB and Compose SQL Server are connection alternatives. Reads and writes use the same context/schema; no CQRS split, outbox, event replication or eventual-consistency mechanism was found.

The desktop exchanges data through WCF. It combines item responses with a global discount response for display, but performs no direct database join and is not a gateway. Catalog images remain desktop filesystem assets whose filenames come from catalog records; their binary data is not stored in the five mapped entities.
